findings.text: Time unit translation helpers convert between tick counts and microsecond millisecond nanosecond and timespec forms in both directions with saturation at defined maxima. Millisecond and microsecond inputs that exceed the representable tick range cap at the maximum offset, with negative millisecond values meaning unbounded wait. Timespec inputs clamp oversized seconds and round partial ticks upward, while tick to timespec splits total nanoseconds with a single division.

User clock translations map kernel ticks and nanoseconds to user visible ticks and back with all ones returned on overflow. Compile time relations between kernel rate tick length and user rate select between direct scaling and scaled division paths, with documented tradeoffs in precision and multi decade overflow horizon for uncommon rates.

Calendar translation covers seconds since epoch to broken down date and the reverse using proleptic Gregorian rules with February placed last for leap purposes. The forward direction normalizes a caller offset into day bounds, derives hour minute second and weekday from a Thursday epoch anchor, then resolves year month day and yearday through a March anchored computational calendar that unifies leap and common years.

Small normalization helpers truncate a signed nanosecond count to legacy seconds plus microseconds and add two second plus nanosecond values with normalization, saturating to the largest representable second with zero subseconds on unsigned second overflow.

Cycle to time accumulation provides a monotonic nanosecond total derived from masked cycle deltas with fractional carry preserved across calls. Precision mask derives from configured shift and start timestamp is caller supplied, with stored cycle marker and accumulated total advanced on each read.

Monotonic raw boot tai real and coarse readers expose a family of clocks at nanosecond and second granularity. Latch based fast paths serve monotonic boot tai and real values without blocking, with boot and tai formed by adding stored offsets to fast monotonic. Sequence guarded paths combine stored base and offset with live or cached deltas, raw uses unadjusted base, and a resolution helper reports nanoseconds per cycle from current scaling.

Paravirtual notification management registers and unregisters caller blocks on a shared chain under exclusive timekeeper guard, refreshing exported time data on registration. Exclusive access itself is offered through paired interrupt saving acquisition and restore helpers bound to the core instance.

Primary state pairs a sequence guard with active and shadow keepers plus a raw guard, replicated per keeper index with an alias for the core slot. Fast access uses a latch guard around duplicated read bases, both preloaded from a shared descriptor naming a suspend aware source with full width mask unity gain and zero shift, each fast instance kept on its own cache line.

Clocksource replacement preserves accumulated time while recomputing cycle and nanosecond intervals from nominal rate, rescaling fractional carry on shift changes, resetting error and discipline state, and recording both a disciplined tick length and a constant correction for rounding between intended tick and whole cycles, plus auxiliary conversion factors for coupled event hardware when configured.

Date arithmetic follows Gregorian leap rules where quadrennial years count except centuries unless quadricentennial. February length is base plus leap increment, April June September and November have thirty days and the rest thirty one. Advancement steps within month, then across months, then across years with yearday reset.

Calendar validation sweeps a symmetric eighty thousand year interval around epoch in daily increments, checking converted year month day and yearday against an independently advanced reference and reporting mismatches with year month day yearday and absolute day context under a single slow case registered in a named suite.

Mutation holds the core raw guard with interrupts saved, covering chain updates and paired lock helpers. Steady state readers sample under sequence retry around base offset and delta, fast readers retry around duplicated latch bases, and wide offset translation may use a single atomic load while narrow builds retain sequence protection.

Keeper advancement distinguishes a periodic tick mode that consumes elapsed cycles from a frequency change mode that reprograms rate without tick accounting. Associated update flags separately request clearing of discipline state and recording that the clock was stepped, with a combined value covering both.

Public timing entry points include fast monotonic boot tai and real readers plus raw and second granularity readers and paravirtual registration, suitable for callers needing nonblocking or non instrumentable access to current time without holding keeper guards.

Overflow is handled by saturation to maximum offset or all ones instead of wrap, while generic scaled paths accept tiny relative error in exchange for long overflow horizons. Several readers warn if used while suspended, and the early clock freezes at its suspend snapshot during suspension to avoid stepping across resume.

Update control uses bit zero for clearing discipline state and bit one for clock stepped indication with a combined mask for both. Time subdivision defines hour seconds as sixty times sixty and day seconds as hour value times twenty four.
A cache isolated atomic holds a monotonic floor, a default off static branch gates an inlined counter read path, and a mostly read flag records suspended state.
Auxiliary keeper setup and auxiliary clocksource refresh are inert inline operations when auxiliary support is not enabled.

Counter sampling prefers a hardware snapshot method when the current source offers one and otherwise falls back to plain read. Real seconds are also readable through a single atomic load usable from non instrumentable context.
